summary: The candidate captures the paper's main mathematical arc and all four central external or terminal theorems: Lickorish–Wallace, Kirby calculus, the Turaev ribbon-graph functor, purification, and the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant. Its principal formulas, including the ribbon Hopf conventions, quantum trace, Kirby-color sum, and selected RT normalization, agree closely with the Gold reference. The artifact is nevertheless a raw overlapping pool rather than a clean entry set: several entries have duplicate IDs, a number of Gold lemmas and propositions are downgraded to definitions or absorbed into larger statements, and important supporting results such as handle-slide invariance and blow-up invariance are not independently extracted. A few statements also lose convention-sensitive distinctions or source attribution.
strengths: Faithfully extracts the central surgery, Kirby-calculus, ribbon-category, ribbon-Hopf, modular-category, purification, and RT-invariant results.
Preserves the Gold convention theta_V=rho_V(v) and the quantum-trace formula Tr_V(rho_V(uv) composed with f).
Provides generally plausible page locators and recognizable theorem or definition names.
Includes useful supporting material beyond the minimum Gold coverage, such as categorical trace, pivotal structure, linking-matrix signature, and root-of-unity truncation.
issues: Duplicate raw entries reuse identical IDs for duality, ribbon category, categorical dimension, and the Turaev ribbon-graph theorem; the tensor-product action and purification theorem also appear in near-duplicate forms under different IDs.

The Gold handle-slide invariance lemma, blow-up invariance lemma, Kirby-presentation-independence proposition, and Kirby-reduction proposition are not extracted as distinct entries; their content is only partly implicit in the final RT theorem.
Several structural Gold claims are misclassified as definitions: coproduct-induced monoidality, antipode-induced duality, R-matrix braiding, and quantum-trace/categorical-trace compatibility.

The standalone Hopf algebra definition, standalone twist definition, finite simple system/domination definition, purification definition, and negligible-morphism definition are absent or only embedded in broader entries.

The dual-module entry presents both S and S^{-1} formulas as alternative actions on V* without explaining the left-versus-right dual convention, weakening mathematical precision relative to the Gold ambient convention.
The colored framed-link invariant is typed as a definition and does not clearly state the Gold proposition's ribbon-isotopy invariance under the general End_C(1)=K hypothesis.
Classic external results are recognizable by name but lack explicit source-attribution metadata comparable to the Gold references.
The RT theorem contains the unexplained notation D_circ while the surrounding entries use D, creating a minor convention and transcription inconsistency.
